# E123 -- Tate

## Metadata
- **Brand**: Tate (Tate Museums)
- **Industry**: Arts / Museums
- **Document**: Tate Brand Guidelines (v1)
- **Year**: 2010 (modified 2013)
- **Pages**: 24 (A3 landscape spreads)
- **Designer/Agency**: Tate Design Studio (internal)

## Brand Strategy
- **Mission**: "Promote public understanding and enjoyment of British, modern and contemporary art" -- democratise access to art.
- **Brand idea**: "Tate provokes dialogue" across five platforms, between artists, audiences, and institutions.
- **Five platforms**: Tate Britain, Tate Modern, Tate Liverpool, Tate St Ives, Plus Tate (partner organisations).
- **Brand values**: Open, Diverse, International, Entrepreneurial, Sustainable.
- **Invitation**: "Look again, think again, join in" -- both an invitation and a challenge to respond, debate, and participate.
- Foreword by Nicholas Serota (Director).

## Logo
- Dynamic logo system with multiple variations reflecting the brand's dynamic approach to audience engagement.
- Core logo plus platform-specific logos (Tate Britain, Tate Modern, Tate Liverpool, Tate St Ives, Plus Tate).
- Positive and negative logo families provided.
- Logo may be reproduced in any colour from the Tate colour palette on corporate materials; creative materials may use other colours with Design Studio approval.
- **Exclusion zone**: minimum clear area equal to the height of the word "Tate" on all sides.
- Departments and companies (Tate Members, Tate Entertaining, etc.) use the core Tate logo -- no new logos created. Department names written in Tate typeface, bold sentence case, positioned well away from logo.
- Programmes (Tate Shots, Tate Kids, Tate Film, Young Tate, etc.) also use core Tate logo; programme names in Tate typeface with creative freedom for programme content illustration.

## Typography
- **Custom typeface**: Tate -- "modern, clear and distinctive," used for all signage and communications.
- **Four weights**: Ultra Thin, Thin, Regular, Bold -- each with italic variants (8 styles total).
- No prescribed rules on weight selection -- "choose the one which best fits your message."
- Used for all internal signage and external communications.

## Color
- Large, vibrant palette (16 colours) designed to keep the brand "exciting and lively" and to "create different moods, to surprise and challenge":
  - White (#FFFFFF), Black (#000000)
  - Pantone Yellow C (#FFEE00), Pantone 389C (#CEE007)
  - Pantone 3115C (#46C3D3), Pantone 354C (#009279)
  - Pantone 2735C (#2800AF), Pantone 253C (#9D4793)
  - Pantone Orange 021C (#F78F1E), Pantone Red 032C (#EF4135)
  - Pantone 806C (#FF0093)
  - Pantone Warm Grey 10C (#8A7967), Pantone Warm Grey 5C (#BFB6AD)
  - Pantone 7543C (#BBC0C4), Pantone 7545C (#51626F)
- CMYK and RGB breakdowns are custom (not standard Pantone defaults) -- users instructed to follow specified values exactly.

## Graphics
- Not covered beyond the logo system itself. No graphic devices, patterns, or illustration guidelines documented.

## Photography
- Not covered in this document. The guidelines focus exclusively on logo, typeface, colour, and written style.

## Applications
- References to: membership cards, menus (Tate Entertaining), marketing leaflets (Families), web pages (Tate Kids), booklets (Tate Going Green).
- Online Visual Style Guides referenced as a separate document from Tate Design Studio.
- Application examples shown inline with logo usage guidance rather than as a dedicated section.

## Tone of Voice
- **Written style** section with specific house rules:
  - "Tate" only -- never "the Tate" or "Tate Gallery."
  - Date format: Monday 23 September 2010 (no ordinals).
  - Numbers: write out up to 100; percentages written out ("ten percent").
  - Time: 24-hour clock with full stops (19.00, not 19:00).
  - Telephone: 020 7887 8888 format (space after area code).
  - Artwork captions: Artist Name, Title, Year -- no brackets or commas.
  - Open punctuation throughout (no commas in dates/addresses, no full stops after abbreviations).
- Full Written Style Guides referenced as a separate Tate Design Studio document.

## Outliers
- Dynamic logo system with flexible colourway application is ahead of its time for 2010.
- Custom typeface (Tate) with 8 styles but zero prescriptive hierarchy rules -- unusually open for a museum brand.
- The "Do not" page (p.19) likely contains misuse examples but text not fully extractable.
- Brand strategy section (brand idea, platforms, values, invitation) is notably clear and well-articulated for an institutional document.
- Interactive PDF with clickable navigation (AcroForm).

## Quality Score
3.5 / 5
Strong brand strategy articulation and a distinctive identity system with custom typeface and expansive colour palette. However, the guidelines are relatively brief (24 pages) and lack depth on photography, graphic language, digital applications, and tone of voice beyond house style rules. The flexible, low-prescription approach suits an arts institution but limits utility as a standalone production guide.
